subject: math.LO
name: Vaught conjecture
statement: Is it provable in ZFC that every first-order theory in a countable language has either at most countably many countable models up to isomorphism or exactly continuum many?
importance: A foundational model-classification problem linking logic and descriptive set theory.
status_note: The continuum hypothesis implies the displayed dichotomy; whether ZFC proves it remains open. This is not presented as a known independent statement.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Vaught conjecture

subject: math.LO
name: Martin conjecture: Borel dichotomy
statement: For every Borel function f:2^N→2^N respecting Turing equivalence, is there a Turing cone on which f is constant up to Turing equivalence, or a cone on which x is Turing reducible to f(x) for every x? A cone consists of all reals computing one fixed real.
importance: Predicts a canonical form for definable operations on degrees of computability.
status_note: This is the first part of the Borel version, formulated in ZFC; uniform and order-preserving special cases are known.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Martin conjecture: Borel dichotomy

subject: math.LO
name: Reverse-mathematical strength of Fraïssé’s theorem
statement: Does the subsystem ATR₀ of second-order arithmetic prove that countable linear orders are well-quasi-ordered by embeddability, meaning that every infinite sequence L₀,L₁,… has i<j with L_i embedding into L_j?
importance: A major test of the exact axioms needed for infinite structural theorems.
status_note: Fraïssé’s assertion itself is Laver’s proved theorem; the open question concerns its proof strength. It implies ATR₀ over RCA₀ and follows from Π¹₁-comprehension.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Reverse-mathematical strength of Fraïssé’s theorem

subject: math.LO
name: Tarski’s exponential-function problem
statement: Is the first-order theory of (R,+,×,<,0,1,exp), with the usual real exponential function, decidable: does an algorithm determine the truth of every sentence in this language?
importance: Asks whether effective real algebraic reasoning extends to exponentiation.
status_note: O-minimality and model completeness are known; decidability is conditional on an appropriate Schanuel conjecture and remains unproved unconditionally.

references.title: Berarducci and Gallinaro: On the elementary theory of the real exponential field (2026)

subject: math.LO
name: Kolmogorov–Loveland versus Martin–Löf randomness
statement: Does every infinite binary sequence on which no computable nonmonotonic betting strategy can gain unbounded capital satisfy every Martin–Löf randomness test? Such a test is a uniformly effectively open sequence U_n with fair-coin measure at most 2^(-n).
importance: One of the central unresolved equivalence questions in algorithmic randomness.
status_note: Martin–Löf randomness implies Kolmogorov–Loveland randomness; the converse is open.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Kolmogorov–Loveland versus Martin–Löf randomness

subject: math.LO
name: Π¹₁-conservativity of Ramsey’s theorem for pairs
statement: Does adding Ramsey’s theorem for pairs and two colors to RCA₀+BΣ⁰₂ prove no new Π¹₁ sentences beyond RCA₀+BΣ⁰₂? Ramsey’s theorem states that every two-coloring of unordered pairs of natural numbers has an infinite homogeneous set.
importance: A central question about the logical strength of elementary infinite combinatorics.
status_note: Related conservativity statements with stronger induction or weaker sentence classes are proved; this precise version remains open.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Π¹₁-conservativity of Ramsey’s theorem for pairs

subject: math.LO
name: Weiss’s amenable-action question
statement: Does every Borel action of a countable amenable group on a standard Borel space have a hyperfinite orbit equivalence relation, that is, an increasing union of Borel equivalence relations with finite classes?
importance: Connects measurable group dynamics with the structure of definable equivalence relations.
status_note: Many classes of amenable groups are covered; measure-theoretic hyperfiniteness does not settle the everywhere-Borel assertion.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Weiss’s amenable-action question

subject: math.LO
name: Stable fields conjecture
statement: Is every infinite field whose first-order theory in the language of rings is stable separably closed, meaning it has no proper finite separable algebraic extension?
importance: A key proposed classification of fields by model-theoretic tameness.
status_note: The assertion is known for large stable fields; ω-stable and superstable fields satisfy stronger conclusions.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Stable fields conjecture

subject: math.LO
name: Cherlin–Zilber algebraicity conjecture
statement: Is every infinite simple group of finite Morley rank isomorphic to the group of points of an algebraic group over an algebraically closed field?
importance: A proposed extension of algebraic-group classification into abstract model theory.
status_note: Small Morley-rank and even-type cases are proved; the general finite-rank assertion remains open.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Cherlin–Zilber algebraicity conjecture

subject: math.LO
name: Superpolynomial lower bounds for Frege proofs
statement: Are Frege propositional proof systems not polynomially bounded: for every polynomial p, is there a tautology of length n whose shortest Frege proof has length greater than p(n)?
importance: A central lower-bound problem in proof complexity and efficient formal reasoning.
status_note: Lower bounds for restricted propositional systems do not establish superpolynomial lower bounds for general Frege systems.

references.title: Open Problems in Mathematical Logic: Superpolynomial lower bounds for Frege proofs
